Header: Xanthomonas campestris pv. musacearum Ye enset atewlagi beshita

Prevention: Use disease free planting material which is available from the
Center or from an area not affected by the disease
Put fencing around the field to stop animals entering as they can spread the disease
The disease survivies in the soil so expose planting holes to sunlight for at least one week before planting new plants
Sterilise cutting implements by flaming with alcohol or washing with sodium hypochlorite (bleach solution) after cutting a diseased plant to avoid spreading the disease to other plants
Do not plant new plantlets in areas where the disease has occurred in the past
Monitoring: Check for symptoms of the disease from the seedling stage then at weekly intervals
The first symptoms to appear are wilting and yellowing of the top leaves
When the disease advances, yellow/ cream coloured ooze (bacterial) can be seen inside the stem when it is cut
Take action straight away when the first symptoms are noticed: wilting and yellowing of the top leaves
Direct Control: Remove the whole plant from the ground and bury in a deep hole located outside of the field
Prepare a hole by digging out enough soil to accommodate the infected plants
Cut the plant parts so they fit into the hole and then cover with soil
Restrictions: There are no chemical direct controls for this disease
